title: Graceful region affinity with capacity-feedback steering and staged circuit-breakers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Improve multi-region request routing to reduce tail latency and minimize cross-region egress while maintaining availability for high-priority customers. Current geo-pin heuristics are binary and create hard failovers that cause capacity hotspots and unnecessary long tails during partial outages. Goal: implement a soft-affinity routing layer that combines token-aware localness, live capacity feedback, and staged per-tenant circuit-breakers to gracefully degrade to remote regions only when necessary.
design_notes:
Core components:
1) Soft-affinity score: compute per-request affinity using token ownership (customer token / project id), recent regional success rate, and measured p95 latency delta. Scores are continuous (0..1) rather than binary pins.
2) Capacity feedback loop: every region exposes a capacity pulse containing current free concurrency slots, recent acceptance rate, and predicted 60s tail risk. Router ingests these at 1s cadence and demotes affinity when capacity low.
3) Staged circuit-breakers: three stages - warm (traffic percentages diverted), hard-shed (reject with guidance), and fallback (route to remote hot-standby). Breakers are per-tenant and per-model variant, with throttle budgets enforced for P0 customers.
4) Latency SLO integration: routing decisions include SLO weight for key accounts. Customers near SLO burn get soft-priority escalation to local capacity.
5) Safety: include hysteresis windows and short-term trial hedging to avoid flip-flop.
Architecture: router proxy (edge) implements scoring and consults regional capacity service (aggregator) via gRPC. Policy engine returns action: local-accept, local-hedge, remote-route, reject.
Implementation notes: start with read-only scoring in canary region to log decisions; then enable fast-path for low-risk traffic; finally enable per-tenant budgets and breaker enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: Router computes soft-affinity score for 100% of traffic in canary and logs differences vs current geo-pin policy
When a region reports capacity below threshold, affinity score demotes and traffic diverted such that local region QPS reduces by >=30% within 30s in controlled test
Staged circuit-breaker transitions exercised in chaos tests (network partition + CPU spike) and do not cause >1.5x p99 increase for remaining healthy tenants
No SLO regressions for top-10 P0 customers during progressive rollout; alerting for any p50/p95/p99 degradations triggers automatic rollback
Operational dashboards (per-tenant routing actions, capacity pulses, breaker state timeline) available in Console and linked in PRD
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Telemetry-only run in staging and canary region for 2 weeks. Phase 1: Enable soft-affinity for <10% of non-P0 traffic in eu-west-1 with read-through fallback. Phase 2: Expand to 30% and enable warm breaker stage for selected customers. Phase 3: Enable full enforcement for non-critical workloads and observe 72h. Phase 4: Gradual expansion to all regions and P0 customers with negotiated budgets and manual approval. Each phase gated by automated SLO checks and manual kill-switch.
monitoring_and_slos: Expose metrics: affinity_score_distribution, region_capacity_free_slots, breaker_state_count, routed_remote_pct_per_region, tenant_slo_burn_rate. SLOs impacted: p95 generation latency target 200ms for regional-local requests, p99 target 400ms; additional safety objective: remote-route rate <5% for majority of tenants. Set alerts for sudden increase in remote-route or breaker transitions exceeding thresholds.
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: oscillation between regions causing instability. Mitigation: implement hysteresis windows and trial hedging before commit.
Risk: inaccurate capacity pulses leading to over-shedding. Mitigation: smooth signals and fall back to historical capacity curves when telemetry missing.
Risk: uneven customer experience during rollout. Mitigation: per-tenant budgets and opt-out flag for enterprise customers until SLA agreements in place.
Risk: added decision latency at edge. Mitigation: inline scoring light-weight, cache last decision for identical prefixes for 100ms.
Risk: complexity in debugging route decisions. Mitigation: add per-request reason code and trace id to logs and Console trace panel.
Risk: security review for cross-region control plane calls. Mitigation: use mTLS and token-scoped authorization and request audit logs.
